name: @epoch/adapter-renderer-threejs
description: Epoch Three.js Embedded Interactive Renderer adapter (W058, ACR-007/X2.0) — the FIRST real interactive renderer behind the frozen W056 RendererAdapter seam (@epoch/renderer-fabric, contracts/renderers v1.1.0): mounts the canonical W016 WorldScene projection into a real Three.js scene graph (every Object3D carries its semantic entity id; renderer-native state is disposable presentation), hit-tests raw pointer input through the real Three.js Raycaster into semantic entity ids and normalizes it into the EXISTING typed Epoch world-interaction intent vocabulary (@epoch/world-experience — select/inspect/isolate/hide/measure/annotate/zoom/pause/resume/follow-agent; never a parallel vocabulary, never a durable write), drives orbit/pan/zoom camera controls as presentation-only state, applies state overlays/highlights/focus decorations/layer visibility/visible agent markers, executes declared typed degradations (reduced-fidelity/static-frame/wireframe) and fidelity budgets, captures portable snapshots, restores portable view state across switches, and tears down every GPU resource it created (geometries, materials, textures, renderer; disposed sessions refuse everything). The GL-dependent path (WebGLRenderer construction, frame image capture) is an INJECTED surface — the default is headless (Node 22, no GPU): the scene graph, camera math, Raycaster hit-testing, input normalization, degradation, snapshot/restore, and disposal are fully testable without a GL context; honest browser GL evidence is W061's E2E surface. Three.js is a CAPABILITY behind the adapter, never authority (capability-foundation policy CF1.0; engine imports live ONLY in this package).
